relevance_note: This cross-sectional study of 425 patients with monogenic autoinflammatory disease reports its HA20 patients only as a group ("HA20 (n=14)") and as counts, e.g. "eosinophilic gastroenteritis (EGE) was diagnosed in 2 patients (HA20 and HIDS)", with no label, age, sex, variant or other individual-level detail for any HA20 patient.
method_note: Read the whole Markdown by hand; no script transcribed a table. HA20 data appear only as cohort percentages (Table 1, Table 2, Figures 1-4) and as counts. Two sentences each single out one unnamed HA20 patient by one feature: EGE ('eosinophilic gastroenteritis (EGE) was diagnosed in 2 patients (HA20 and HIDS)') and flare-related perioral swelling ('one patient each with DADA2, HA20, and CANDLE'). I treated these as counts (n=1 of 14), not as identifiable individuals: the paper gives no further detail, and it does not say whether they are the same person or two people, so rows would risk inventing or merging a person. Hence reports_individuals_with_tnfaip3_variant = false and the person-level tables are empty. The supplementary section lists only file titles, with no content. Inconsistencies in the paper: cohort counts in the text (FMF n=118, TRAPS n=73, HIDS n=38, total 425) differ from Table 1 'Identified (total)' (FMF 117, TRAPS 72, HIDS 39; these sum to 424); HA20 is 14 in both. Some HA20 percentages in Table 1 imply a denominator of 13, not 14 (e.g. 'Sex (% M)' 30.8%, colchicine at time of analysis 23.1%). Protocol numbers differ between Methods (94-HG-0104, 10-I-0148) and Results/Ethics (94-HG-0105, 10-I-1048). cites_prior_report_of_same_patients left null because the paper says nothing about earlier reports of its patients.

year.span: Journal: Annals of the rheumatic diseases (2021)

study_type.span: In this cross-sectional study, clinical data were assessed in 425 AID patients using questionnaires and chart reviews

span: Smaller cohorts with PAPA (n=18), HA20 (n=14), CANDLE (n=14), and SAVI (n=12) were also followed
All patients carried a molecular diagnosis of MEFV, NLRP3, TNFRSF1A, ADA2, MVK, PSTPIP1, TNFAIP3, proteasome genes, or STING1 disease-causing variants
